articles.title: Travis Kelce’s Six Flags investment faces another blow as California’s Great America announces its final season amid profitability concerns

articles.body: Travis Kelce, the 37 year old tight end, has been focusing on his career on the field while one of his investments has continued to land in trouble in the last few months. As the Kansas City Chiefs look to bounce back on the field after consecutive losses, Travis Kelce’s investment in Six Flags faces a new hurdle.Travis Kelce backed Six Flags faces a closure of the iconic park as the company faces low profitability and legal issuesA few hours ago, the star tight end Travis Kelce’s investment in Six Flags is facing a new issue as the company has announced that the California's Great America in Santa Clara, California, will permanently close on Labor Day, September 6, 2027, after operating for more than five decades.In a statement to PEOPLE, Dave Vosejpka, park manager of California’s Great America, said, “For more than five decades, this Santa Clara theme park has brought people together, created family traditions and served as the backdrop for unforgettable memories…”Dave Vosejpka, park manager of California’s Great America, added, “The Farewell Season is an opportunity for generations of Bay Area guests to return, spend time with family and friends, and revisit the attractions and traditions that have made the park in Santa Clara, California, such a meaningful part of the community.”According to the New York Post’s recent report, the closure of the park is linked to the low profitability that Six Flags have been facing for the last few months.New York Post’s recent report reads as, “Executives told investors that Great America ranked near the bottom of the company’s portfolio in profit margins, with the high cost of operating contributing to the decision not to renew the lease.”However, Six Flags has not confirmed the speculations yet as the company continues to remain involved in a number of legal issues.Six Flags’ website read as, “From iconic rollercoasters and family attractions to the kid-sized fun of Planet Snoopy and the splash-filled excitement of South Bay Shores Waterpark, guests can enjoy a full day of unforgettable experiences all with one admission…In 2027, the park celebrates its Farewell Season, offering one final opportunity to experience a Bay Area tradition before its final day of operation on Labor Day 2027.”The announcement has now sparked a number of different emotions among fans as Six Flags have also found themselves in controversial legal issues.Six Flags witnessed a tragic death and brutal injuries as Travis Kelce keeps himself awayJust last month, a 42 year old school teacher from Atlanta was ejected from his seat in Six Flags Georgia and died a tragic death.Even before that, there had been many speculations about Six Flags’ safety. Amid all the mess, Travis Kelce has kept himself away from the mess after investing in the company last year.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: New York Giants vs. Philadelphia Eagles NFL Week 9 Live Updates, Highlights, and Analysis
articles.summary: The Philadelphia Eagles host NFC East divisional rival, the New York Giants. A battle between two teams that are heading in different directions.
articles.body:
The Giants outlasted the Eagles with a 19-11 victory. The Giants close out the game with a sack, which is quite apropos, given that both defenses dominated the opposing offensive lines.

The Giants' two-quarterback system combined for 18 of 27, 198 yards and a touchdown. Joe Milton went 18 of 34, threw for 169 yards, and added 64 yards on the ground.

Philly's supporting cast dropped four of Milton's passes, and Elijah Mitchell made a mind-numbing decision to stay inbounds instead of getting out to stop the clock. Self-inflicted wounds hurt the Eagles' chances of winning this game.

This game was won and lost in the trenches. Both defensive fronts dominated their matchups and bullied their way into the backfield all game.

The Giants continue their winning ways, going to 5-2-1, and the Eagles fall to 2-7.

articles.standfirst: El quaterback de los Bengals lleva a su equipo a la victoria con una actuación memorable en el Madrid Game
articles.summary: El quaterback de los Bengals lleva a su equipo a la victoria con una actuación memorable en el Madrid Game
articles.body: Mismo lugar, pero distinto escenario. El Santiago Bernabéu se volvió a disfrazar con los colores de la NFL, por segundo año consecutivo. Dejó a un lado las mágicas noches de Champions para dar paso a las épicas tardes de 'touchdowns'. Pero hay cosas que nunca cambian. Y una de ellas fue el baño de masas previo al partido que se dio Florentino Pérez. El presidente del Real Madrid se dio una vuelta de honor a pie de césped, durante el calentamiento, como el creador que contempla su obra. Como el emperador que saluda al público del Coliseo Blanco. Aunque esta vez, estaba teñido de naranja. Los Atlanta Falcons, que ejercían de locales, fueron abucheados durante todo el partido por la Who Dey Nation. Ante un Bernabéu a rebosar (78.660 espectadores, 50 más que el año pasado), los Bengals dieron la patada de inicio y el cuadro de Atlanta recibió el balón para atacar por primera vez. Un drive inicial que iba a servir como anticipo de lo que nos depararía la tarde. Con un estelar Bijan Robinson, los locales movieron cadenas de manera cómoda, hasta que Michael Penix Jr. le puso la guinda al drive en forma de pase a Charlie Woerner. Apenas habían transcurrido unos minutos y ya teníamos el primer 'touchdown' en el marcador. Era un aviso de que el encuentro no iba a ser como el del año pasado, donde hubo que esperar a la segunda mitad para la primera anotación de 6 puntos. Era el turno de los Bengals, capitaneados por un Burrow que dejó claro desde el principio que no había venido a Madrid a hacer turismo. Con el ovoide en el medio campo, el de Iowa plantó sus dos pies, enfocó y disparó un pase teledirigido que flotó sobre el cielo del Bernabéu, sabiendo que tenía como destino final las manos de Ja'Marr Chase de camino a la zona de anotación. Dos ataques, dos 'TD'. Los de Atlanta no pudieron seguir el ritmo al cuadro de Cincinnati que convertía cada posesión en touchdown. Incluso el propio Burrow se llevó su propia anotación de carrera. Al descanso, el marcador lucía un abultado 10-24, con 3 'TD' de Burrow y más de 200 yardas. En la segunda parte, como suele ser habitual, vimos unas defensas más ajustadas. Los Falcons le pusieron picante al encuentro con un gran drive que acabó en touchdown de Bijan Robinson. Pero no tardaron los visitantes en arruinar cualquier intento de remontada. Esta vez, y por segunda ocasión, fue Higgins quien recibió el 'regalo' dentro de la 'end zone'. Tanto el '5', como Ja'Marr Chase (10 recepciones para 155 yardas y un 'TD') fueron los principales compañeros de baile de un Burrow que, 'simplemente', se dedicó a ponerle sinfonía a cada ovoide que lanzaba. Entramos al último cuarto con un todavía voluminoso 17-31. Los locales tuvieron la oportunidad de recortar tres puntos, pero el field goal de Folk se fue por el lateral. Sí que ampliaron la cuenta los 'tigres', con otra patada de McPherson. A los Falcons se les acababa el tiempo, y no les quedaba otra cosa que arriesgar. Y como es habitual, tomar riesgos no suele acabar bien. A falta de cuatro minutos para el final, Michael Penix Jr. lanzó la primera y única intercepción del encuentro tras un mal pase a la espalda de Bijan Robinson. Burrow, apenas tuvo que volver a ponerse la armadura, el partido ya estaba finiquitado. Ya había hecho su labor. Una labor que concluyó con 4 'TD' y más de 270 yardas. 17-34, así finalizó el segundo Madrid Game. Un partido que, esta vez sí, nos enseñó lo que es la NFL, ese deporte que reina en Estados Unidos y que ha llegado para quedarse en España.

articles.title: Ya conocíamos el show, hoy nos presentaron el deporte
articles.standfirst: La contracrónica del Falcons-Bengals celebrado en el Bernabéu
articles.summary: La contracrónica del Falcons-Bengals celebrado en el Bernabéu
articles.body: Volvió la NFL a Madrid. Es cierto que su retorno al Santiago Bernabéu había pasado relativamente desapercibido entre la Champions, el tenis, la F1, la MotoGP, LaLiga... Pero eso era más bien una sensación, un sentimiento que se esfumaba nada más pisabas la Castellana. El Bernabéu volvía a enamorar a la NFL, que esta vez trajo un auténtico partidazo, que se saldó con victoria de los Bengals. "Es un estadio más americano que europeo", comentó el director de campo de la NFL esta semana, tras visitar el Bernabéu. Lo cierto es que cuesta creer que alguien piense que es buena idea no celebrar aquí la final del Mundial. El estadio enamora tanto como la ciudad. Aunque la verdad es que hoy no toca ese debate, aunque da qué pensar. Ya conocíamos el show, pero este año descubrimos el deporte. Ese que enamora en América y que aquí aún no ha cautivado... aún. Lo que es seguro es que con partidazos como este Falcons-Bengals, están más cerca de hacerlo. Un encuentro cargado de estrellas, jugadas para el recuerdo y mucha diversión. ¿Habrá conseguido el Real Madrid más seguidores en EEUU tras este partido? Posiblemente sí, más aún tras la vuelta de honor de Florentino Pérez en la previa del partido. Preguntaba el presidente del Madrid a una aficionada si era merengue. Lo hacía entre autógrafos, fotos y saludos a la multitud. (Por cierto, la chica dijo que era del Barça). El Bernabéu a explotar y ni un solo incidente. El comportamiento de los aficionados a la NFL fue ejemplar... y eso que se vendía cerveza. Al considerarse un evento-espectáculo, la normativa permitía que los seguidores congregados en el Bernabéu amenizaran el partido mientras consumían bebidas alcohólicas. Eso sí, no estaba la cerveza para todos los bolsillos: 8€. Mientras algunos jugadores de LaLiga consideran "una mierda tener que hacer esta entrevista", las estrellas de la NFL atienden a los medios (incluso en el vestuario tras el partido) y los comprenden como parte de su negocio. Por cierto, algunos de los cracks que visitaron el Bernabéu rondan los 50 millones anuales de contrato. La propia organización también lo hace. Lejos de las persecuciones y las trabas a las que esta sujeta la comunicación en gran parte de Europa, para la NFL la prensa no es un mal necesario, es simplemente lo segundo: necesaria.

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes returns to lead Chiefs past Jets after scary hit to right elbow
articles.summary: Mahomes looked like he may have sustained a significant injury but was able to return on the next Kansas City possession.
articles.body:
Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes left Sunday's game against the New York Jets with an injury scare after a hit to his throwing elbow but was able to return to help lead a 35-12 win.

The hit took place in the second quarter on a sack that forced a fumble. Mahomes' right elbow bent awkwardly on the sack, and he fumbled the ball. He was in clear pain after the hit and walked to the sideline holding his right arm. The Jets took over possession after recovering the fumble.

But Mahomes was able to throw on the sideline and returned to the field before the end of the half after the Chiefs retook possession of the ball.

Kansas City took over with 32 seconds remaining in the half after a missed Jets field goal and Mahomes was able to complete a 12-yard pass, then scramble for seven yards to set up a Harrison Butker field-goal attempt just before the end of the half.

Butker missed the 51-yard attempt, and the Chiefs went into halftime with a 14-12 lead.

"He hurt his elbow a little bit," head coach Andy Reid told CBS at halftime. "It's sore, but he came back. He's a tough kid."

Mahomes continued to play to start the third quarter and led the Chiefs to a touchdown drive on their first possession of the half to extend their lead to 21-12. The Jets didn't mount a challenge from there.

Mahomes didn't appear to be impacted by the injury scare and finished the day completing 23 of 31 passes for 278 yards (7.8 yards per attempt) with 2 touchdowns and no turnovers.

The Chiefs improved to 6-2 with the win and remain a half game in the AFC West behind the Denver Broncos, who improved to 7-2 with a 26-21 win over the Carolina Panthers.

articles.summary: Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes avoided a major injury after appearing to suffer an arm injury in the second quarter of Sunday's 35-12 win against the New York Jets, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.
articles.body:
Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes avoided a major injury after appearing to suffer an arm injury in the second quarter of Sunday's 35-12 win against the New York Jets, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.

Mahomes was visibly favoring his right arm after Jets rookie David Bailey got to him in the pocket. He walked off the field holding the arm:

Mahomes was nonetheless back for Kansas City's next offensive drive.

Mahomes discussed the injury after the game, indicating there might be some further issues:

Kansas City coach Andy Reid said he expects Mahomes to be "sore" on Monday:

The good news is, however, that it's reportedly not a serious injury.

In his nine seasons as the Chiefs' starter, the 31-year-old has won three Super Bowls, five AFC titles and two NFL MVP awards while making the Pro Bowl on six occasions. His 283.7 passing yards per game also rank first all time. Kansas City has also gone 117-37 overall (17-4 in the playoffs) with him starting under center.

Last year was a tough season for Mahomes. His 2025 campaign ended in Week 15 after suffering a torn ACL and LCL in his left knee against the Los Angeles Chargers on Dec. 14. Mahomes immediately underwent surgery and began rehab.

However, rehab went very well, and he met his stated goal of returning in time for the Chiefs' season opener, a 31-10 win, over the Denver Broncos on Sept. 14.

This year has been great for Mahomes, who has thrown for 1,795 yards, 12 touchdowns and four interceptions.

The Chiefs remade their quarterback room over the offseason outside Mahomes. Justin Fields, who has started games for the Chicago Bears, Pittsburgh Steelers and New York Jets, is now the team's top backup.

Garrett Nussmeier, who starred at LSU before going in the seventh round of this year's draft, is also aboard as the third-stringer.

articles.summary: J.J. McCarthy left the Giants-Eagles game with a hip injury after a hit from Zack Baun, forcing New York to turn the offense back to Jameis Winston.
articles.body: J.J. McCarthy had two basic issues during his time with the Minnesota Vikings: Ability. And durability. Since his trade to the New York Giants, McCarthy has shown no ability problems because he beat out Jameis Winston as the team's starter and even provided something of a spark in helping New York beat the Houston Texans in overtime. So no ability issue. But Sunday presented a durability issue. McCarthy left the game against the Philadelphia Eagles with what the team is saying is a hip injury. articles.title: Cowboys survive after wild CeeDee Lamb catch and fumble late in win over Colts
articles.summary: CeeDee Lamb's 48-yard reception was negated by a late fumble, which nearly ruined things for the Cowboys on Sunday afternoon.
articles.body:
Luckily for the Dallas Cowboys, CeeDee Lamb's wild catch-turned-fumble late on Sunday afternoon didn't cost them the game at Lucas Oil Stadium.

The Cowboys beat the Indianapolis Colts 27-23 after a game-winning touchdown from Javonte Williams in the final two minutes. But it was a sequence with Lamb earlier in the fourth quarter that could have cost them the contest.

Lamb made an incredible catch in the fourth quarter, and managed to complete the grab while just barely staying in bounds right up against the sideline. But instead of completing the play, Colts rookie cornerback Kenneth Harris didn't actually touch Lamb.

So Lamb jumped up and ended up with a 48-yard play, deep into Colts territory. But as Lamb was tackled, he actually lost the ball going down. That gave the ball right back to Indianapolis after a review.

It looked like that was going to cost Dallas the game, too. The Colts made it all the way down into scoring position, thanks to three major penalties — including a 40-yard pass interference call on DaRon Bland.

But inside the red zone, Quinnen Williams forced a huge fumble to give Dallas the ball right back and stop what could have been a go-ahead touchdown drive.

Eventually, it was Williams' touchdown that pushed Dallas ahead for good and gave it the four-point win.

Dak Prescott went 21-of-34 for 335 yards with two touchdowns in the win, which pushed the Cowboys to 4-5 on the season. They are in second in the NFC East race, behind only the New York Giants. Lamb had 195 yards and a touchdown on 10 catches. He found the end zone in the second quarter on a 44-yard catch.

The Cowboys will take on the San Francisco 49ers next week.

articles.title: Shedeur Sanders' Comeback Falls Short in Browns-Saints, Box Score Stats, Highlights for Shough, More
articles.summary: Shedeur Sanders and the Cleveland Browns came up short in overtime against Tyler Shough and the New Orleans Saints.
articles.body:
Shedeur Sanders and the Cleveland Browns came up short in overtime against Tyler Shough and the New Orleans Saints.

New Orleans stopped the Browns on a two-point conversion in overtime to claim a 23-22 win over the Deshaun Watson-less Browns.

Forty-three of the game's 55 points were scored in the fourth quarter and overtime. Sanders engineered a game-tying drive to send the contest to overtime. However, the Browns couldn't make one final play in the extra period to grab the win.

New Orleans won the game with a stop on a two-point conversion on the second possession of overtime.

The Browns scored their touchdown in overtime on an incredible individual effort from Harold Fannin Jr.

Unfortunately for the Browns, they were unable to add two more points to finish off a wild fourth quarter and overtime.

New Orleans scored first in overtime on a Shough pass to Juwan Johnson.

The majority of regulation didn't feature much offensive excitement.

The game finally came to life with five minutes left in the fourth quarter, when Sanders hit K.C. Concepcion on a 64-yard touchdown pass.

Shough and the Saints answered right back with a six-play, 55-yard drive that concluded in an Audric Estime touchdown run.

Sanders rallied the Browns on a game-tying drive that sent the game to overtime.

Sanders hit Jerry Jeudy on a 30-yard pass down the left sideline to get the Browns close to field goal range.

Andre Szmyt knocked in a 51-yard field goal a few plays later to add an extra period to the game.

The loss dropped the Browns to 5-4. Three of their four defeats this season have come in the last five weeks. They face the Houston Texans in Week 10.

New Orleans moved to 3-5 and it plays the Carolina Panthers next week in a NFC South battle.

articles.title: NFL Week 9 Winners and Losers: Puka Nacua saves the Rams, who need to add someone to help him
articles.summary: Myles Garrett returned and had three sacks in a close Rams win.
articles.body:
Puka Nacua is great. He is doing things early in his career that have never been matched before.

The fatal flaw for the Los Angeles Rams might end up being that Nacua is all they have in the passing game.

Nacua was phenomenal again on Sunday in a grind-it-out 20-13 win over the Washington Commanders. He had 14 catches for 150 yards on 19 targets with the go-ahead touchdown in the fourth quarter. Nacua also ran it twice for 20 yards. Nobody else on the Rams had more than 20 yards receiving. Nacua had 150 yards and everyone else combined had 78. That's not an ideal formula, no matter how incredible Nacua is as a player.

The Rams weren't completely whole on Sunday. They played without cornerback Trent McDuffie and tight end Terrance Ferguson, among others. Davante Adams is out with a hamstring injury and could be out until late in the season, which is why the Rams have so few options at receiver. But they did have Myles Garrett back . And Garrett, like Nacua, was great. He had three sacks, including a big 12-yard sack with with the game still in doubt late in the fourth quarter. Los Angeles' defense held on, getting a stop on the final play in their own territory. The Rams still had key players out, but every team in the NFL is dealing with some injuries. The San Francisco 49ers, who lead the NFC West, can attest to that. The Rams just haven't been what everyone thought they would be yet, even though they are getting wins against overmatched teams.

But they are 5-4, which is why the trade deadline is very important for them. Los Angeles has already sold some of its future on trades for Garrett and McDuffie, and it's a team that probably needs another move or two to get back to the status of Super Bowl favorite. Particularly at receiver. Nacua needs some help.

In the third quarter Stafford forced a pass into Nacua despite Nacua being bracketed closely. Safety Nick Cross had an easy interception. It was a clear case of Stafford forcing it to his only receiver option, no matter what. It was Stafford's ninth interception this season, surpassing last year's total already. That type of play showed why the overreliance on Nacua in the passing game needs to be addressed.

It doesn't help that Stafford is dealing with an elbow injury. He has not been able to complete passes downfield in Los Angeles' past few games. It could be argued that the Rams having one option at receiver and playing three tight ends more than half of their plays is what's sapping the offense of its explosiveness, but Stafford's elbow doesn't help either. Their longest play on Sunday, against a bad Commanders defense, was 21 yards.

Perhaps Adams returns from a serious injury and fills the need the Rams have, but that's a gamble for a receiver who will turn 34 on Dec. 24. It also assumes Nacua, who has a long history of injuries and is taking a lot of punishment with all of the touches he's receiving, stays healthy all season. If Nacua goes down, the Rams' passing game will be in real trouble.

The Rams can celebrate their third straight win after a disappointing 2-4 start. But it's clear that they need to be making calls before Tuesday's trade deadline if they want to reach their peak this season.

Here are the rest of the winners and losers from Week 9 of the NFL season:

The Broncos and their good fortune: The Denver Broncos are catching every break this season. And they simply can't lose in one-score games.

The Broncos were trailing 14-13 and the Carolina Panthers had first-and-goal at the 1-yard line when they got one of the most fortunate interceptions you'll see, and it turned the game around. The Panthers decided to throw on first-and-goal. The pass was heading for the ground only to be tipped in the air by tight end Tommy Tremble. Broncos safety Devon Key made a great play to realize the ball was still live and pluck it out of the air before it hit the ground . A challenge and a review showed it was a clean interception. That was a big turning point in a 26-21 Broncos win.

The Broncos got going after that. They scored two straight touchdowns to take a two-score lead. But Denver doesn't play easy games. The Panthers scored and then forced a punt after a pitch to Broncos running back Jonah Coleman was fumbled for a big loss. But Denver hit Bryce Young, who fumbled, and Denver recovered with 1:15 to go. It was another win for the Broncos in a one-score game, their 16th in a row in one-score games. That sets an NFL record which they tied last week when they held on in the final seconds against the Chiefs. The Broncos are 7-2, and piling up wins in close games. Per usual, they had some serendipity on their side.

Jameis Winston: Winston didn't start on Sunday but came up with the key drive the New York Giants needed to get past the Philadelphia Eagles.

Winston came in when J.J. McCarthy briefly left the game after taking a hard hit to his side . Winston got one full drive and made it count. On the drive he completed 6-of-7 passes for 71 yards and a touchdown to Isaiah Likely. Winston also ran for 11 yards. Offense was a struggle for the Giants all game but Winston did his job. It was the Giants' only touchdown in a 19-11 win, their first road win at Philadelphia since 2013. They improved to 5-2-1.

Winston was benched for McCarthy as the Giants chase a division title in the terrible NFC East. But he might have been their most important player on Sunday, coming through when nothing else was working for New York's offense.

Kenneth Walker III: After a couple of quiet games against very good defenses, Walker got an easier assignment on Sunday. And he took advantage of it.

Walker scored two touchdowns on catches and another on the ground as the Chiefs' offense broke out in a 35-12 win over the New York Jets. He rushed for 102 yards and had another 41 receiving. It hadn't been easy for the Chiefs on the road against the Seahawks and Broncos the past two weeks, and Walker in particular was stymied. He was on a blistering pace early in the season but had just 105 rushing yards and no touchdowns the past two weeks. On Sunday he was back to his form of the first few weeks when he was getting buzz as a potential MVP candidate. The Chiefs are 6-2, and still very much in the mix for an AFC West title as long as Walker continues to play well.

Joe Burrow for MVP: The Atlanta Falcons were one of Burrow's toughest matchups in November. All he did was to 18 of 22 for 239 yards with two touchdown passes and one rushing TD. And that was just the first half.

Burrow's MVP push continued on Sunday in Madrid, Spain, as he threw for 271 yards and three touchdowns in a 34-17 win over the Atlanta Falcons. He probably could have put up even bigger numbers but the Bengals were up by double digits for most of the second half. The NFL Network broadcast repeatedly talked about how Burrow told them in production meetings how confident he feels and how healthy he is. It shows.

The Bengals are 6-2 and in good shape to win the AFC North, which is usually a prerequisite for winning MVP. He is putting up monster numbers. He hasn't won before and there will be some sentiment to recognize him with his first MVP award as he turns 30 years old. By the end of November he could be the clear favorite, though Josh Allen, Brock Purdy and Caleb Williams are also in the race. But Burrow is looking like the league's MVP.

Malik Willis: The whole season is a tryout for Willis, who has to prove he's worthy of being the Miami Dolphins' quarterback of the future. Sunday wasn't a good day for him.

Facing a Detroit Lions defense that isn't good and was down multiple starters due to injury, the Dolphins never reached the end zone. Willis was inaccurate on many passes. The Lions were surprisingly quiet on offense too but it didn't matter. Miami couldn't score enough to keep up and lost 19-9. Willis was 13 of 25 for 128 yards and an interception against a Lions defense that was 29th in yards per game allowed coming in.

Willis has had some decent moments, and he has to be graded on a curve because of the lack of talent around him. But he wasn't good enough on Sunday.

Deshaun Watson: Shedeur Sanders couldn't come up with the two-point conversion he needed to close out the win over the New Orleans Saints. But he might have given the Browns a reason to consider a quarterback change.

Sanders, who threw a go-ahead 64-yard touchdown to K.C. Concepcion late in the fourth quarter and also led a game-tying field goal drive in the final seconds of regulation, hit tight end Harold Fannin Jr. for a 39-yard touchdown in overtime after the New Orleans Saints scored first, with Fannin making a great play after the catch. But the Browns threw incomplete on the two-point conversion that would have won the game (there was also a holding call on the Browns) and the New Orleans Saints held on to a 23-22 win.

The loss stung but Sanders played well, as Watson sat out due to being in the concussion protocol during the week. Watson has mostly played poorly and the Browns have been winning in spite of it. Sanders had 297 yards and two touchdowns against the Saints with multiple clutch drives. It will at least be worth considering a change after that.

Sauce Gardner: Gardner's presence on the Indianapolis Colts is a constant reminder of the collapse of the franchise.

Last season, when the Colts were 7-2, Indianapolis traded two first-round picks and receiver Adonai Mitchell for Gardner, an elite cornerback. But Gardner has been mostly hurt with the Colts, who have fallen apart since the middle of last season. And on Sunday, with a chance to beat the Dallas Cowboys, Gardner got beat for the biggest play of the game.

Ryan Flournoy, playing a bigger role with George Pickens out, beat Gardner for a 46-yard catch late in the game when the Colts led 23-20. That set up a go-ahead rushing touchdown from Javonte Williams and the Cowboys defense closed out the win when rookie safety Caleb Downs picked off Daniel Jones, who had another rough day. Dallas held on for a 27-23 win.

The Colts' fall is far from Gardner's fault, but he hasn't helped and the Colts paid way too much for him. Him giving up the game-changing catch to Flournoy was just another reminder of how costly that trade was.

articles.title: Burrow powers Bengals to Madrid win as Chiefs shine despite Mahomes injury scare
articles.summary: Joe Burrow sparked Cincinnati over Atlanta in Spain for a fourth consecutive NFL victory while Patrick Mahomes overcame an injury scare on Sunday to lift Kan...
articles.body:
Joe Burrow sparked Cincinnati over Atlanta in Spain for a fourth consecutive NFL victory while Patrick Mahomes overcame an injury scare on Sunday to lift Kansas City over the New York Jets.

Burrow completed 24-of-29 passes for 271 yards and three touchdowns and ran for another touchdown in Cincinnati's 34-17 triumph over the Falcons at Madrid.

The Bengals improved to 6-2, moving level with idle Pittsburgh atop the AFC North division.

"The sky is the limit when we play like this. This is how we need to attack every game going forward," said wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase, who made 10 catches for 155 yards and a touchdown.

"Intense impact," Burrow said of Chase. "He was unbelievable."

Burrow leads the NFL with 2,386 passing yards and 23 touchdowns.

"He does a good job getting out of the pocket and making scramble plays, keeping the play alive," Chase said. "That's why he's one of the best."

At Kansas City, three-time Super Bowl champion and two-time NFL Most Valuable Player Mahomes suffered a right arm injury and lost a fumble in the second quarter after being sacked by Jets rookie defender David Bailey.

Mahomes threw for 120 yards and two touchdowns to give the Chiefs a 14-12 halftime lead, with coach Andy Reid saying Mahomes hurt his elbow.

Returning in the second half, Mahomes directed touchdown drives of 60 and 82 yards in the third quarter and 57 yards in the fourth as Kansas City beat the Jets 35-12.

Mahomes completed 23-of-31 passes for 242 yards and two touchdowns while Kenneth Walker ran 18 times for 102 yards and a touchdown and caught four passes for 41 yards and two touchdowns for the Chiefs (6-2).

The Denver Broncos became the first NFL team with seven wins as Bo Nix threw for 237 yards and two touchdowns in a 26-21 triumph at Carolina in a matchup of division leaders.

The Broncos (7-2) stretched their win streak to five games despite Bryce Young throwing for 276 yards and three touchdowns for Carolina.

Dak Prescott threw for 335 yards and two touchdowns while Javonte Williams ran for 101 yards and scored the deciding touchdown on a one-yard run with 68 seconds remaining to give Dallas a 27-23 victory at Indianapolis.

New Orleans edged visiting Cleveland 23-22 in overtime on Tyler Shough's 15-yard touchdown pass to Juwan Johnson.

Cleveland's Shedeur Sanders tossed a 39-yard touchdown pass to Harold Fannin with one minute remaining in the extra period but a two-point conversion pass to take the lead failed.

Matthew Stafford threw a seven-yard touchdown pass to Puka Nacua for the winning points and the Los Angeles Rams' defense stopped Washington in the final seconds for a 20-13 road victory.

Rams linebacker Myles Garrett, who set an NFL record for quarterback sacks last season, returned after suffering a knee injury in the opener and made three sacks as well as forcing a fumble.

Jahmyr Gibbs rushed for 74 yards and scored the only touchdown on an eight-yard run in Detroit's 19-9 victory at Miami, the Lions improving to 6-2.

Dominic Zvada kicked four field goals to lift the New York Giants to a 19-11 victory at Philadelphia.

San Francisco will try to reach 7-1 in a later home game against Las Vegas while Chicago will seek a 7-2 start when Tampa Bay visits. Later games also include Houston at the winless Los Angeles Chargers, Green Bay at New England and Arizona at Seattle.

articles.title: Jordan Love's 100th career passing TD puts Packers up 14-0
articles.summary: Jordan Love is the fifth quarterback in Packers history to throw 100 touchdown passes while with the team.
articles.body:
Jordan Love is the fifth quarterback in Packers history to throw 100 touchdown passes while with the team.

Love's 100th came on a five-yard toss to wide receiver Matthew Golden in the first quarter of Sunday's game against the Patriots. The score pushed the Packers' lead to 14-0 with eight minutes to play in the opening quarter.

Love joins Bart Starr, Lynn Dickey, Brett Favre and Aaron Rodgers in the Packers' century club. He also ran 13 yards for the first Packers score of the day.

Golden also had catches of 16 and 49 yards to set up the touchdown. Those are all three of Love's completions on the day and they've been productive ones.

articles.title: Streaking Detroit Lions, blunders doom Miami Dolphins
articles.summary: Playmakers were snails sliding through fresh concrete Sunday as the Detroit Lions scraped by the Miami Dolphins for their fourth consecutive win.
articles.body:
MIAMI GARDENS, Fla., Nov. 8 (UPI) -- Playmakers were snails sliding through fresh concrete Sunday as the streaking Detroit Lions scraped by the Miami Dolphins for their fourth consecutive win.

Fans waited nearly 44 minutes of game time for the lone touchdown of the defensive duel -- a third-quarter run from running back Jahmyr Gibbs -- as the Lions triumphed 19-9 in Miami Gardens, Fla.

"I told them, as a coach, there are things we need to clean up," Lions coach Dan Campbell said at his postgame news conference. "We can be much better. We created some of our own issues at times. Ultimately, we played pretty good defense."

The Lions, who allowed 29.6 points per game through their first five contests this season, surrendered an average of just 13.6 in three contests since their Week 6 bye.

"We've cleaned a lot up," Campbell said. "Guys are trusting what they are being taught. They are executing it. With that execution comes confidence."

Lions defenders consistently bothered Malik Willis on Sunday with dynamic pressure, forcing awkward attempts and denying the Dolphins quarterback of a rhythm.

Dolphins defenders also limited the Lions, who entered the matchup with the NFL's top offense.

"I'm proud of the defense," Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley said. "Certainly, as a competitor, I thought we could have made some more plays at the end. ... Maybe their best performance of the year against, in my opinion, the most explosive offense in the NFL."

All of the Dolphins' points came courtesy of three Zane Gonzalez field goals. The tight tilt featured two successful fake punts for first downs, six sacks and eight field goals attempts.

The Dolphins (1-7) were doomed by an inconsistent passing game, a turnover, untimely penalties and other errors, including a missed Gonzalez field goal attempt. The sluggish performance dropped them to 0-4 at home this season.

The Lions (6-2) used their balanced attack to establish early control. They took 6:36 off the clock on the game's opening drive, which ended with a Jake Bates field goal.

Gonzalez tied the score at the end of the quarter with a 34-yard kick. Bates split the uprights with a 40-yard attempt right before halftime to give the Lions their second lead, which they would not surrender.

Bates made his third field goal on the Lions' first drive of the second half. Gonzalez answered with a 52-yard kick on the next drive. But Gibbs scored his 8-yard touchdown on the next drive to give the Lions insurance.

Bates and Gonzalez each connected on additional field goals in the fourth quarter. Neither team sniffed the end zone over the final 16:19.

Gibbs logged 74 yards and a score off 20 carries. Lions wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown totaled a game-high 86 yards off eight catches. Quarterback Jared Goff completed 17 of 25 passes for 170 yards and an interception.

Defensive end Derrick Moore sacked Willis twice in the win. Safety Chuck Clark snagged his first interception since 2021.

"I thought, defensively, they did a good job against us," Goff said. "Played with good depth, made us keep the ball underneath. ... They did a good job. We certainly had our opportunities to blow it open a little sooner than that and didn't take advantage of them."

Willis completed just 13 of 25 passes for 128 yards and an interception. Rookie cornerback Chris Johnson recorded the first interception of his career in the loss.

The Lions will face the New England Patriots (5-3) on Nov. 15 in Munich. The Dolphins will play the Indianapolis Colts (2-6) on Nov. 15 in Indianapolis.

articles.title: Myles Garrett shows Rams why they traded for him in return vs. Commanders
articles.summary: The star pass rusher was all over the field.
articles.body:
Myles Garrett's career with the Los Angeles Rams got off to a rough start, as he had a bad game in Week 1 and then missed the next seven games with an injury. However, the real Garrett finally arrived in Los Angeles in Week 9.

As the Rams beat the Washington Commanders 20-13 on Sunday afternoon, Garrett's performance was a big reason why. The pass rusher made several huge plays that reminded everyone why Los Angeles acquired him from the Cleveland Browns .

Now that the Rams are 5-4, they have a runway for success down the stretch to shake off a slow start. Garrett's return should only ignite this defense as the team looks to once again make a push for a Super Bowl in the playoffs.

Here's how Garrett dominated against Washington.

Garrett made three plays on Sunday, but they were all huge as they went for sacks on quarterback Jayden Daniels. In fact, his first one even went for a strip-sack, as Garrett forced the turnover on Daniels at the end of the first half.

Garrett's second sack came to start the fourth quarter, with the Rams up seven points on the Commanders. Daniels dropped back on 2nd-and-9, but the pass rusher got to him for a big loss to make the third down an even tougher task.

Finally, Garrett's third sack helped Los Angeles ice the game away, as he got to Daniels on 3rd-and-5, which led to a Commanders turnover on downs.

All of a sudden, the Rams trade for Garrett once again looks good. Not only did Garrett play a huge role in Los Angeles improving to over-.500 for the first time this season, but the pass rusher's three sacks also surpassed Jared Verse's total in the process.

Verse was, along with multiple first-round picks, the focal point of the package that went from the Rams to the Browns in the Garrett deal. However, Verse has no sacks this season despite playing in all nine Saints games.

Now that Garrett looks healthy, he has a chance to be one of the most impactful players in the NFL during the second half.

articles.title: Jayden Daniels throws for 274 yards, TD
articles.summary: Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels completed 24 of 35 passes for 274 yards, one touchdown and no interceptions in Week 9

Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels completed 24 of 35 passes for 274 yards, one touchdown and no interceptions in Week 9 against the Los Angeles Rams , while running four times for 16 yards.

articles.title: NFL history made as Lions and Dolphins punters achieve feat not seen since 1981
articles.summary: The Detroit Lions unsurprisingly came away from their clash with the Miami Dolphins as winners on Sunday, and made NFL history in the process. During their 1...
articles.body:
The Detroit Lions unsurprisingly came away from their clash with the Miami Dolphins as winners on Sunday, and made NFL history in the process.

During their 19-9 win, Jack Fox made an 11-yard pass after faking a punt in the second quarter. It was a trip down memory lane for the Lions punter, who threw for 18 touchdowns during his high school career in Missouri.

A pass from a punter is not a super rare occurrence. That came when his opposite number, Bradley Pinion, repeated the feat in the fourth quarter. He threw an even more impressive 46-yard pass, finding Kaytron Allen in open grass for a 1st & 10.

It's just the second time both punters have completed a pass in an NFL game since 1950, with the last such instance occurring 45 years ago. That was Cowboys vs Lions.

The Dolphins won't be all that thrilled by their part in making NFL history this weekend. They came into Week 9 second from the bottom in the power rankings, only better than the Chargers.

The offense gave Miami very little to work with. Malik Willis finished 52% on his throws for 128 yards and an interception, and he was sacked three times. Caleb Douglas led the receivers with six catches for 70 yards, but he let a fourth-down pass slip through his hands in the final quarter. Miami was flagged 11 times in all.

Sloppy football like that won't get you far against a team as strong as Detroit. Hafley's team is now 1-7.

articles.title: Dan Quinn 'Not Happy' with Questionable Final Play in Commanders' Loss to Rams
articles.summary: The Washington Commanders' season has been defined by late-game blunders, and they committed another in Sunday's loss to the Los Angeles Rams.
articles.body:
The Washington Commanders' season has been defined by late-game blunders, and they committed another in Sunday's loss to the Los Angeles Rams.

Despite being just past the Rams' 30-yard line in the final seconds, the Commanders opted to go for a short pass followed by a handful of laterals rather than just aiming for the end zone.

After the game, head coach Dan Quinn said he was "not happy with the execution of that play."

The poor ending to Sunday's game continued a trend for the Commanders this season.

In Week 5 against the New York Giants, Washington had the ball in field goal range late in overtime after forcing a fumble on the other end and appeared to be on its way to a victory.

But quarterback Jayden Daniels took a sack and was unable to get back to the line of scrimmage to stop the clock, and the game ended in a tie.

"The sequence of that does not fall on him," Quinn told reporters about the play. "It's an out-of-bounds throw or a 'clock'. That has to come from me."

The following week, against the San Francisco 49ers, the Commanders trailed by six points and had the ball in the final minute with good field position. They marched down to the 28-yard line with seconds remaining, but an intentional grounding call moved the ball back to the 40.

Washington then failed to get off a pass attempt as Daniels was sacked as time expired.

The Commanders are now 2-5-1 as their playoff hopes continue to dwindle, but they still have a path to the postseason thanks to a weak NFC East.

They can't afford to continue making the kinds of errors they made on Sunday, though.

"We have to play all three phases together," Quinn told reporters . "I've seen too much of it where it's part of it, not the whole thing. That's what we're gonna continue to practice, and that has to click. It just has to. Too far along to not have it all working together."

articles.title: New Daniel Jones Trade Rumors Update Colts QB's Future Ahead of 2026 NFL Deadline
articles.summary: Daniel Jones is reportedly staying with the Indianapolis Colts.
articles.body:
Daniel Jones is reportedly staying with the Indianapolis Colts.

According to Tom Pelissero of the Ringer and Netflix Sports, the team told the quarterback that he will not be traded prior to the NFL trade deadline:

Pelissero's report comes after Jones sidestepped a question about whether he's contemplated asking for a trade following the team's 27-23 loss against the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday, its fifth straight defeat.

"Just so much going on here with getting ready for this game and playing well today, that's plenty to think about," he told reporters.

Jones, 29, hasn't exactly put his best foot forward this season. On Sunday he finished 20-of-34 for 180 yards, a touchdown and an interception, taking two sacks. He now has six touchdowns, 10 interceptions and 24 sacks taken on the year.

The Colts, meanwhile, are in an absolute free fall and are clearly open for business after already trading away guard Quenton Nelson and defensive lineman DeForest Buckner. Trade rumors have circulated around other players on the team, including Jones and star running back Jonathan Taylor.

On Saturday, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network and Adam Schefter of ESPN reported that the Colts have "received calls from multiple teams inquiring about trading for Jones" and that the team had been "willing to listen to any offers."

The Baltimore Ravens were reportedly one of the teams that inquired before landing Jacoby Brissett.

As for the financial repercussions on both sides of any Jones' trade, Mike Ginnitti of Spotrac noted that an acquiring team "takes on approximately $3 million in remaining 2026 compensation, followed by a substantial $38 million in 2027 ($10.5 million guaranteed for injury). That's roughly $41 million in total remaining cash obligations, excluding incentives. Indianapolis would gain $7.4 million in immediate cap savings while leaving behind $11.8 million in dead cap for 2026. The Colts would also save another $11.6 million against the cap in 2027, despite carrying $35.2 million in dead cap."

Not exactly ideal numbers for either side, especially when it involves a player who isn't particularly performing at a high level this season.

And while things could still change before Tuesday's deadline, it appears Jones will be staying in Indianapolis for the rest of the season.

articles.title: Myles Garrett Reacts to Return from Injury in Rams' Win to Jayden Daniels, Commanders
articles.summary: After being sidelined for the last seven weeks due to knee surgery, Los Angeles Rams star edge rusher Myles Garrett made his long-awaited return to the lineup on Sunday against the Washington Commanders.
articles.body:
After being sidelined for the last seven weeks due to knee surgery, Los Angeles Rams star edge rusher Myles Garrett made his long-awaited return to the lineup on Sunday against the Washington Commanders.

Garrett appeared to be in top form, recording three sacks and a forced fumble as the Rams earned a 20-13 victory to improve to 5-4. He's now the first Rams player to have three or more sacks in a single game since his teammate Aaron Donald in 2021.

"Honestly, it means so g--damn much. This is the kind of adversity that I really haven't faced in my pro career," Garrett told Fox Sports' Jennifer Hale after the game.

Garrett also told reporters after the game that he felt a sense of relief to produce the way he did on Sunday.

"It was a weight off my shoulders, just getting back to where I am," he said. "I'm nowhere near where I want to be as far as, like, my performance and things I know I can do and how I can move, but this is a confidence booster for sure."

After a quiet start to the game, Garrett made his presence felt in the second quarter when he got to Commanders star quarterback Jayden Daniels and knocked the ball loose for the strip-sack. Omar Speights recovered the fumble, giving the Rams a chance for a field goal before halftime.

Garrett then recorded his second sack early in the fourth quarter to help preserve Los Angeles' lead.

Garrett got to Daniels for the third time on a late third down to end Washington's comeback attempt.

The Rams entered Sunday's game ranked near the bottom of the league with just 12 sacks, as they surely felt Garrett's absence. His return could help Los Angeles regain its footing on defense just in time for the playoff race.

Garrett and the Rams will try to keep up their strong play as they look to extend their win streak to four straight games in their Week 10 NFC West matchup against the Arizona Cardinals.

articles.title: Shedeur Sanders Denies Shading Saints in Viral Video, Offers Apology After Browns Loss
articles.summary: The Cleveland Browns made a change at quarterback for Sunday's game against the New Orleans Saints out of necessity, as Deshaun Watson was sidelined after he spent time in the concussion protocol during the week.
articles.body:
The Cleveland Browns made a change at quarterback for Sunday's game against the New Orleans Saints out of necessity, as Deshaun Watson was sidelined after he spent time in the concussion protocol during the week.

That meant Shedeur Sanders made his first start of the season, and it was quite the performance for the Colorado product.

On paper, he went 19-of-31 for 297 yards, two touchdowns and zero interceptions in the dramatic 23-22 overtime loss.

After the game, he made sure to say that he was not trying to shade the Saints defense with his comments earlier in the week and offered an apology "if my words were taken out of context."

Sanders made headlines in the days leading up to the game after discussing what he saw on film:

Sanders will surely be thinking about the play he didn't make at the end when the Browns went for two and the win after Harold Fannin Jr.'s touchdown just for Sanders to throw an incomplete pass.

Despite the incompletion, he was impressive in crunch time with a 64-yard go-ahead TD pass to KC Concepcion in the fourth quarter and then a field-goal drive that included taking a massive hit from Chase Young and still delivering a strike to Jerry Jeudy to set up Andre Szmyt's field goal to force the overtime.

Here's what he had to say about the play after the game:

He also had the touchdown pass to Fannin in overtime and played much better in the second half.

After all, it was anything but an ideal start for Sanders, who threw for an ugly 38 yards in the first half as the visitors scored three points. While he didn't turn the ball over, he appeared to turn the wrong direction on a 4th-and-goal play from the 1-yard line.

The confusion on the handoff led to Quinshon Judkins being stuffed, which was the type of mistake the struggling offense couldn't afford to make on the road.

However, Sanders set up a go-ahead field goal in the third quarter when he unleashed a deep ball to Denzel Boston, who made an adjustment and an incredible catch while high-pointing the ball.

It was part of a much better second-half from the quarterback, as he appeared to get more comfortable as the game progressed.

This comes after Watson and Sanders battled for the top position on the team's depth chart in training camp before the former eventually earned the No. 1 spot. Through the first eight games, the 31-year-old starter completed 65.5 percent of his passes for 1,806 yards, seven touchdowns and three interceptions.

He also went 5-3 in those starts, which put the Browns in the AFC playoff race in the early going.

As for Sanders, he is in the midst of his second season with Cleveland after he was selected with a fifth-round pick in the 2025 NFL draft.

He suited up in eight games as a rookie, including seven starts. Sanders completed 56.6 percent of his passes for 1,400 yards and seven touchdowns to go along with 10 interceptions.

The 24-year-old also played in two preseason games this year, finishing 15-of-22 for 153 yards and one touchdown while getting picked off twice.

articles.title: Puka Nacua Injured on Final Play for Rams vs. Commanders, Latest Updates on WR
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Rams finally have a winning record after beating the Washington Commanders on Sunday, but the victory also came with some bad news.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Rams finally have a winning record after beating the Washington Commanders on Sunday, but the victory also came with some bad news.

Per ESPN's Adam Schefter, star wide receiver Puka Nacua suffered a knee injury on the final offensive snap of the 20-13 win and will undergo an MRI on Monday. According to Schefter, the team believes Nacua did not suffer a torn ACL.

The injury came after a monster day for Nacua, who hauled in 14 receptions for a season-high 150 yards and a touchdown, marking his third consecutive game finding the end zone.

Nacua stayed healthy last year en route to the best season of his career, in which he recorded 1,715 yards and 10 touchdowns, but injuries struck early on in the 2026 campaign.

After playing in the first game of the season against the San Francisco 49ers in Melbourne, he missed Weeks 2 and 3 against the New York Giants and Denver Broncos, respectively, because of a groin injury.

Despite having to miss two games, Nacua has put together another strong season, recording 715 yards and four touchdowns on 70 receptions.

Another injury to Nacua would be a major blow to a Rams offense that is already without one of its key players.

Veteran wide receiver Davante Adams landed on the injured reserve after Los Angeles' Week 6 matchup against the Arizona Cardinals. The initial timeline for his return was six to 10 weeks, though head coach Sean McVay said in late October that Adams is expected to return "on the shorter end" of that frame.

Assuming he makes a swift recovery, he'd likely be back on the field by early October.

When healthy, the pairing of Nacua and Adams is one of the best in the league and gives the Rams arguably the scariest offense in the NFL. Los Angeles is finally getting things going after winning three straight games, and it will look to keep the momentum going with or without its top two receivers.

articles.title: Shedeur Sanders makes case to replace Deshaun Watson despite Browns' overtime loss to Saints
articles.summary: Shedeur Sanders threw for 297 yards and two touchdowns against the Saints, but his receivers did much of the heavy lifting in Cleveland's OT loss.
articles.body: For most of Sunday's game, Shedeur Sanders looked a lot like Deshaun Watson (with regard to his play, not the ... other stuff). But a few key plays, including one of the best throws of Sanders' young career to help set up a game-tying field goal, are likely to have Browns fans demanding that the team turn the keys over to the 24-year-old son of Pro Football Hall of Famer Deion Sanders. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE Sanders finished 19-of-31 for 297 yards, two touchdowns and no interceptions in Cleveland's 23-22 overtime loss to the New Orleans Saints. Those numbers look pretty good, but they also make his afternoon look quite a bit better than it actually was. Which, again, sounds a lot like Watson's season. Sanders got his first start of the year after Watson entered the concussion protocol during the week. Watson cleared the protocol Saturday, but the Browns still made him inactive Sunday. Head coach Todd Monken had already named Sanders the starter Friday after Watson was unable to participate in team reps during the week. That gave Sanders, who started seven games as a rookie last season, another chance to prove he deserves to be the team's starter moving forward. For much of the afternoon, he didn't do a whole lot with it. Shedeur Sanders had plenty of help on his biggest plays Sanders threw for just 38 yards in the first half and was sacked five times for a loss of 37 yards on the day. After a run went backward, Sanders took a seven-yard sack that pushed Cleveland back to the 12. The Browns settled for a field goal. With Cleveland trailing 9-6 in the fourth quarter, Sanders found KC Concepcion for a 64-yard score. It was a huge play that gave the Browns the lead with 5:21 remaining, but Concepcion was wide open on what appeared to be a blown coverage by New Orleans. Sanders deserves credit for finding the wide-open Concepcion and delivering a catchable ball that gave him room to work. But it was a throw that every NFL quarterback should be able to make. Cleveland then had a chance to run out the clock and win in regulation after its defense forced a punt. Sanders picked up a first down with his legs, but a holding penalty and another sack helped derail the possession. New Orleans got the ball back and scored a touchdown to take a 16-13 lead with 58 seconds left. Sanders delivered his best throw when Cleveland needed it most Facing third-and-6 from his own 30 on the ensuing drive, Sanders moved outside the pocket and fired a 30-yard strike to Jerry Jeudy while taking a massive hit from Chase Young. It was easily his best throw of the afternoon and one of the best of his young NFL career. It was probably the best throw by a Browns quarterback this season, too. Sanders eventually led the Browns into position for Andre Szmyt's 51-yard field goal, which tied the game with eight seconds remaining and forced the game to overtime. The Browns won the toss and elected to kick, something I've repeatedly said is the wrong decision for NFL teams. Cleveland ignored my advice, and New Orleans promptly marched 74 yards in 11 plays for a touchdown. Sanders answered by completing six of eight passes on a 67-yard touchdown drive. Harold Fannin Jr., though, deserves most of the credit for the play that brought Cleveland within a point. Boston's catch, Concepcion's touchdown and Fannin's catch-and-run accounted for 163 of Sanders' 297 passing yards. His receivers did a lot of work to make that final line look as good as it did. Before Sunday's game, Monken said he assumed Watson would remain the starter when healthy. But Watson hasn't exactly done enough to cement his status as the Browns' starting quarterback. articles.title: More proof that any team trading for Daniel Jones at the NFL trade deadline is chasing fool's gold

articles.body: The next thing you'll hear about Daniel Jones is how the Minnesota Vikings or some other team is interested in trading for him before the NFL trade deadline on Tuesday. MINNESOTA VIKINGS' SOFT BENCHING OF KYLER MURRAY LEADS TO CARSON WENTZ TAKING OVER AS NEW STARTING QB Jones plays for the Indianapolis Colts now and continues to be one of the most disappointing and under-performing reasons that team has been in garage sale mode for nearly a month, as losses increased and optimism dropped off the table. You quarterback is Daniel Jones to whom you also committed to this year before he remained healthy and still freakin' helped crash your now 2-7 season. articles.title: Jonathan Taylor Reacts to Possibility of Playing Final Game for Colts Amid NFL Trade Rumors
articles.summary: With the NFL trade deadline nearing, Jonathan Taylor's time with the Indianapolis Colts could be coming to an end.
articles.body:
With the NFL trade deadline nearing, Jonathan Taylor's time with the Indianapolis Colts could be coming to an end.

Taylor said after Sunday's game against the Dallas Cowboys that he doesn't know whether it will be his last with the team, but he gave a heartfelt reaction about the possibility of taking his last snaps with the Colts.

"Well, I think you play every game like it's your last, but at the end of the day, this has been a spot where I grew up," Taylor said. "You go to college, you know, you're a young man, but like, you really grew up, started a family and you really embrace this city, these people, and you're just like, 'This place helped shape me into the man I am today.' I'm very grateful. So, if it is, I'm very grateful for the city of Indianapolis."

Few names have swirled in trade rumors as much as Taylor's over the past few weeks. The Colts, who are 2-7 after Sunday's loss to Dallas, are sellers heading into the deadline, having already traded guard Quenton Nelson and defensive lineman DeForest Buckner.

Taylor is the team's biggest asset, making him the name to watch before Tuesday afternoon.

Earlier this week, Taylor was asked whether he had requested a trade, but did not confirm or deny asking out of Indianapolis.

"At this point, the hay is in the barn now. We're preparing for the Cowboys," he told reporters. "We got a home game. After last week, nothing else matters. We just gotta give these fans a win."

Sports Illustrated's Albert Breer reported on Friday that the New York Giants are a "serious suitor" for Taylor, while previously linked teams like the Denver Broncos and Minnesota Vikings "might be a little less inclined to trade for Taylor now" following previous trade talks.

Giants head coach John Harbaugh said Sunday that the team pulled its offer for Taylor, but is keeping the door open for a potential deal.

"I'm not saying that report's not true. Those conversations are taking place," he told reporters . "If something happens for any player, can't talk about any [specific] player because they're with other teams right now, but we're not ruling anything out."

According to Breer, the Colts are seeking a first-round pick or the "equivalent" of what the San Francisco 49ers gave the Carolina Panthers for Christian McCaffrey in 2022. The Niners sent the Panthers 2023 second-, third- and fourth-round picks, and a 2024 fifth-rounder, in return for McCaffrey.

Taylor would be an upgrade to almost any backfield in the NFL. The 27-year-old has rushed for 656 yards and eight touchdowns so far this year and is well on his way to another dominant season.

Whether he'll be on his way out of Indianapolis after six and a half seasons will become clear in the next few days.

articles.title: The unlikely quarterback who beat a Patrick Mahomes record
articles.summary: The Denver Broncos’ victory was their 17th consecutive win with Bo Nix as the starter in games decided by one score or less — breaking a record held by Patrick Mahomes.
articles.body: Given the freedom to choose any NFL quarterback since 1950 to win your favorite team a close game, you might think of names like Joe Montana, Tom Brady or Patrick Mahomes. What if the best option was technically a divisive third-year quarterback? Week 9 for the Denver Broncos followed what has by now become a familiar pattern. During the first three quarters, Denver trailed, and neither the Broncos nor Nix looked quite comfortable. Then the fourth quarter began, and he made all the right moves — yet again. The Broncos’ 26-21 victory was their 16th consecutive win with Nix as the starter in games decided by one score or less — breaking a record held by Kansas City with Mahomes during the 2023-24 seasons, which had been the longest streak since 1950, including playoffs, per NBC Sports research. “Part of it pisses me off,” Broncos coach Sean Payton told reporters when he was asked about the streak, “because there’s a few of them that you would say shouldn’t have been one-score games.” Payton added that “we still have some work to do.” True to form, Nix didn’t produce all highlights against the Carolina Panthers. In the first quarter, facing third-and-goal from Carolina’s 8-yard line, Nix dropped back to pass ... and kept dropping back to elude blitzers ... then kept running backward until he reached the 33-yard line before he at last threw the ball away. After three quarters, Carolina led 14-13. Nix threw an interception and committed a fumble, though it didn’t lead to a turnover. Yet in fourth quarters, Nix, 26, transforms into an unbelievably effective quarterback at producing plays when they matter most. On Sunday, they included leading two fourth-quarter scoring drives, including a 26-yard touchdown pass to Pat Bryant with 5:41 left that put Denver ahead for good. It was his 13th career fourth-quarter comeback — as many as Hall of Fame quarterbacks Roger Staubach and Steve Young had in their careers. Nix finished with 237 passing yards and two touchdowns. He also completed six of his seven passes on third down for 72 yards and a touchdown. Denver’s five fourth-quarter comebacks are the most in the NFL. “It seems like it’s always the same feeling,” Nix said. “There’s always a look in the huddle like, ‘Hey, guys, we don’t have a choice right here, and we gotta go make something out of it.’ Today, those second-half touchdowns were really, really important.” Nix entered this season under high expectations after he led five fourth-quarter comebacks and seven game-winning drives last season as he helped Denver reach the AFC championship game, a game he couldn’t play in because of an ankle injury. In Week 1, however, the Broncos lost by double digits to Kansas City, and in mid-October, Amazon analyst and former NFL quarterback Ryan Fitzpatrick ripped Nix after a “Thursday Night Football” game for his meek play during — naturally — a narrow Broncos win over Seattle in overtime. “It was really frustrating to watch,” Fitzpatrick said after Nix threw for 107 yards and averaged 4 yards per attempt, the lowest mark of the season to that point. “Part of it for me is Bo Nix is not playing competitively. It’s almost disrespectful to the quarterback position how he’s playing football right now.” Nix said at the time that he didn’t try to play conservatively. “I try to be extremely aggressive when I get the opportunities,” he said. Payton said he never considered benching Nix. The move has paid off. Nix didn’t throw an interception for five straight games until Sunday. Even with that pick, the Broncos won their fifth straight game and improved to 7-2. But whether Denver is ready for legitimate Super Bowl contention remains, like any evaluation of Nix, in the eye of the beholder. “At 7-2, we feel really confident,” Nix said. “But at the same time, there’s a lot of things we can get better at.” Despite the Broncos’ strong record, their offense has been inconsistent all season, leading Payton to take back play-calling responsibilities last month. The inability to find a rhythm outside fourth quarters factored into why Denver had been outgained by 658 yards this season entering Sunday — third-worst in the league. (The Panthers then outgained Denver by 41 more yards.) Denver has been able to wriggle out of those holes all year. Whether it will work in the playoffs is another question. But in 16 consecutive close games with Nix as the starter, Denver has found a formula that is as ugly as it is consistent.

articles.title: Justin Herbert Injured, DJ Uiagalelei Makes NFL Debut as Chargers Fall to 0-8 in Loss to Texans
articles.summary: Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert suffered a finger injury during Sunday's 44-22 loss to the Houston Texans, and the team will now have to wait and see as to what the severity of the injury is.
articles.body:
Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert suffered a finger injury during Sunday's 44-22 loss to the Houston Texans, and the team will now have to wait and see as to what the severity of the injury is.

Head coach Jim Harbaugh said Herbert wanted to come back in the game, but the coaching staff thought better of it.

"Could be a fracture, we'll find out," Harbaugh told reporters .

Hebert said he will do "whatever I can to make sure I'm 100 percent."

While Harbaugh noted Herbert wanted to play through the injury, the coach opted to have DJ Uiagalelei—who made his NFL debut on Sunday—finish the game.

The Chargers quarterback, who went undrafted out of Florida State, came in for Herbert late in the fourth quarter as his team trailed big.

Uiagalelei's first drive ended with a touchdown pass.

Uiagalelei finished his first NFL game with 24 yards and a touchdown on 2-of-7 passing in a 44-22 loss.

It had been another rough day for Herbert before he exited, as he had just 193 yards, a touchdown and an interception, continuing what has been a rough stretch for the veteran.

Herbert came into the game with 1,398 passing yards, five touchdowns and 10 interceptions. Before Sunday, he hadn't thrown a touchdown pass since Week 5.

The prospect of Uiagalelei taking the starting job from Herbert would have sounded like a joke coming into the season, but nothing is out of the realm of possibility amid an 0-8 start.

The Chargers' hopes of reaching the playoffs are essentially over at this point, but bringing in a new starting quarterback could give the team a spark heading into the second half of the season.

Uiagalelei had a five-year college career with Clemson, Oregon State and Florida State, though he never quite lived up to the hype he had coming into college. After going undrafted in 2025, he signed with the Chargers but didn't make the 53-man roster. He spent last season on the team's practice squad.

Over the offseason, he competed for the backup position behind Herbert but ultimately lost to Trey Lance and started the year on the practice squad.

After Lance was placed on the injured reserve with a groin injury in September, Uiagalelei was promoted to the active roster, paving the way for him to serve as Herbert's backup.

It's unclear whether the injury Herbert suffered on Sunday was serious, but if it is, Uiagalelei will have to step up and salvage what is left of the Chargers' season.

articles.title: Chargers fall to stunning 0-8 in listless loss to Texans as pressure mounts on Mike McDaniel, Justin Herbert and Jim Harbaugh
articles.summary: The Chargers entered the NFL season projected to compete for the AFC West. Eight games in, they're just trying to avoid becoming one of the worst teams in NF...
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Chargers entered the NFL season projected to compete for the AFC West. Eight games in, they're just trying to avoid becoming one of the worst teams in NFL history.

A campaign of Chargers futility continued Sunday as they lost in a 44-22 blowout to the Houston Texans that dropped them to 0-8. They finally scored two touchdowns in the fourth quarter, but by then, they were meaningless, and the Chargers never challenged the Texans.

Chargers break TD-less streak, but it was too late to help

Those late LA scores broke a streak of 37 consecutive drives without scoring a touchdown. The Chargers didn't find the end zone in consecutive losses to the Chiefs and Rams prior to Sunday's game. In the process, they passed the 2024 Dolphins, who went 30 offensive possessions without finding the end zone. That team was coached by Chargers offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel.

Sunday's loss will further increase pressure on McDaniel, head coach Jim Harbaugh and quarterback Justin Herbert.

The loss wasn't all about a bad Chargers offense. Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud had a field day, completing 21-of-35 passes for 384 yards with 5 touchdowns and an interception against a sieve of a Chargers secondary. But LA's offense bears plenty of the blame.

Herbert completed 13-of-23 passes for 193 yards with a touchdown and an interception in a passing line that didn't tell the full story. He was sacked a career-high eight times for a combined loss of 40 yards. The sacks repeatedly stunted Chargers drives, including a third-quarter possession that ended with a fourth-down sack and the Chargers trailing 31-9.

The Texans extended their lead to 38-9 before the Chargers made it into the end zone.

Herbert appeared to sustain left hand injury

Herbert, meanwhile, finished his day battered and on the bench. He appeared to sustain an injury to his non-throwing hand late in the game. He emerged from the injury tent with a glove on his left hand and a wrap around one of his fingers.

Harbaugh said the team is checking to see if Herbert suffered a fracture on his middle finger. Herbert told reporters postgame that he doesn't expect the injury to be an issue.

Herbert watched the end of the game from the sideline in favor of backup DJ Uiagalelei. With the game far out of reach, it wasn't immediately clear if Herbert's exit was more about the score or his hand.

Tepid offense takes Chargers out of game early

Prior to their first fourth-quarter touchdowns, Chargers drives on Sunday finished like this: field goal, punt, field goal, field goal, punt, punt, interception, turnover on downs, fumble.

The offense resembled nothing like a unit led by a two-time Pro Bowl quarterback in Herbert or guided by a touted offensive mastermind in McDaniel.

Harbaugh was asked about the offensives struggles at halftime.

"We've just gotta keep digging deep," he told the CBS broadcast. "Dig even deeper. One play at a time. One drive at a time. One play, one life."

They didn't dig deep enough Sunday. They'll have to hope that upcoming games against the Ravens, Jets, Patriots and Buccaneers will provide a window to break into the win column.

Even if they do, it won't ease the pressure on the leaders on the Chargers' sideline and in the locker room.
