Malik Nabers was not a fan of the criticism he received from Fox Sports' Greg Olsen on Sunday.

After Olsen called out Nabers for his body language during the New York Giants' win against the Philadelphia Eagles, the wide receiver took to social media to respond.

Olsen, a Pro Bowl tight end who retired in 2020, discussed Nabers' body language during a touchdown, saying he should be celebrating his teammates rather than worrying about his own stats.

"It's not good," Olsen said on the broadcast (h/t Heavy's Tony Adame ). "There's a fine line between being demanding and chasing greatness and then being a bad teammate … like if your teammate scores a touchdown for the lead and you're still worried about your touches."

Later on in the game, Nabers dropped a good pass from J.J. McCarthy that would have been a touchdown, and he was clearly frustrated afterwards.

"You can't act like that and drop that pass," Olsen said. "That's a perfectly thrown ball."

It was a below-average game from Nabers, who had just 43 yards on five receptions. Coming into the game, he had recorded four consecutive games with 111 or more receiving yards, including a 165-yard performance against the New Orleans Saints.

It's easy to understand why a player of Nabers' caliber would be frustrated with a slow night, but Olsen made it clear that the third-year player needs to stay even-keeled no matter the situation.

Nabers seems to think he did nothing wrong, but it's fair to see why Olsen interpreted him as having bad body language.

articles.title: NFL Week 9 Winners and Losers: Puka Nacua saves the Rams, but now he's dealing with a knee injury
articles.summary: Myles Garrett returned and had three sacks in a close Rams win.
articles.body:
Puka Nacua is great. He is doing things early in his career that have never been matched.

The fatal flaw for the Los Angeles Rams might end up being that Nacua is all they have in the passing game. And now his health is in question.

Nacua was phenomenal again Sunday in a grind-it-out 20-13 win over the Washington Commanders . He had 14 catches for 150 yards on 19 targets with the go-ahead touchdown in the fourth quarter. Nacua also ran it twice for 20 yards. Nobody else on the Rams had more than 20 yards receiving. Nacua had 150 receiving yards and everyone else combined had 78. That's not an ideal formula, no matter how incredible Nacua is as a player.

And then after the game there was some alarming news. Nacua will undergo an MRI on his knee, according to ESPN . The team doesn't believe he has a torn ACL, the report said, but having an MRI means the team has some level of concern.

The results of that test could lead the Rams to get more aggressive at the trade deadline, which is Tuesday. Even if Nacua avoided a serious injury, the Rams have to know that they can't play like they did Sunday, without anyone else contributing in the passing game.

The Rams weren't completely whole in Week 9. They played without cornerback Trent McDuffie and tight end Terrance Ferguson, among others. Davante Adams is out with a hamstring injury and could be out until late in the season, which is why the Rams have so few options at receiver. But they had Myles Garrett back . And Garrett, like Nacua, was great. He had three sacks, including a big 12-yard sack with the game still in doubt late in the fourth quarter. Los Angeles' defense held on, getting a stop on the final play in Rams territory.

Like LA, every team in the NFL is dealing with injuries. The San Francisco 49ers, who lead the NFC West, can attest to that. The Rams just haven't been what everyone thought they would be yet, even though they are getting wins against overmatched teams.

But they are 5-4, which is why the trade deadline is very important for them. Los Angeles has already sold some of its future on trades for Garrett and McDuffie, and it's a team that probably needs another move or two to get back to the status of Super Bowl favorite, particularly at receiver which could be a pressing need if Nacua misses time. Even with him, the Rams have only one option in the passing game.

In the third quarter Stafford forced a pass into Nacua despite Nacua being bracketed closely. Safety Nick Cross had an easy interception. It was a clear case of Stafford forcing it to his only receiver option. It was Stafford's ninth interception this season, surpassing last season's total. That type of play showed why the over-reliance on Nacua in the passing game needs to be addressed.

It doesn't help that Stafford is dealing with an elbow injury. He has not been able to complete passes downfield in Los Angeles' past few games. It could be argued that the Rams having one option at receiver and playing three tight ends more than half of their plays is what's sapping the offense of its explosiveness, but Stafford's elbow doesn't help either. LA's longest play Sunday, against a bad Washington defense, was 21 yards.

Perhaps Adams returns from a serious injury and fills the Rams' need, but that's a gamble for a receiver who will turn 34 on Dec. 24. It also assumes Nacua, who has a long history of injuries and is taking a lot of punishment with all of the touches he's receiving, doesn't get bad news on the MRI or that he stays healthy the rest of the season even if this injury scare isn't bad. If Nacua misses time, the Rams' passing game will be in trouble.

The Rams can celebrate their third straight win after a disappointing 2-4 start, but with some concern over one of their most important players. It's clear they need to be making calls before Tuesday's trade deadline if they want to reach their peak this season. And it could reach a critical level based on Nacua's MRI.

Here are the rest of the winners and losers from Week 9 of the NFL season:

Tank Dell: The feel-good touchdown of the NFL might have happened Sunday in Los Angeles.

Tank Dell hadn't scored since 2024. He missed all of last season with a horrific leg injury, and had played in just one game this season as he continued to recover. Anyone who had forgotten about Dell was reminded of him when he caught a long pass from C.J. Stroud and was running down the sideline for a 63-yard touchdown. That set off a celebration on the Texans' sideline. It was a great moment for Dell, whose career had been in doubt after he tore multiple ligaments in his knee and also suffered a dislocated kneecap.

The Texans got an easy 44-22 win over a Chargers team that is 0-8 and somehow getting worse as the season goes on. Stroud was fantastic on Sunday with 384 yards and five touchdowns. The defense got to Justin Herbert often, forcing him into another rough game. Houston had eight sacks. It was a good win, but will be remembered for Dell's long touchdown, which sealed his comeback from injury.

Drew Lock: At very least, Lock is establishing himself as a reliable backup quarterback. That can lead to a lot of contracts and a long career.

Lock has been called upon to start twice this season and has done his job each time. He had a steady game for the Seattle Seahawks, which was without Sam Darnold due to a quad injury, not turning it over once. That's a perfectly fine formula for the Seahawks, who rely on their defense. With Lock doing enough on offense, the defense clamped down on the Arizona Cardinals and won 17-3.

Lock had 175 yards and a touchdown in the win. He wasn't spectacular. But he didn't make any big mistakes and played an important role in a win, which is all any team asks of its backup quarterback.

The Broncos and their good fortune: Denver is catching every break this season. It simply can't lose in one-score games.

The Broncos were trailing 14-13 and the Carolina Panthers had first-and-goal at the 1-yard line when they got one of the most fortunate interceptions you'll see, and it turned the game around. The Panthers decided to throw on first-and-goal. The pass was heading for the ground only to be tipped in the air by tight end Tommy Tremble. Broncos safety Devon Key made a great play to realize the ball was still live and pluck it out of the air before it hit the ground . A challenge and a review showed it was a clean interception. That was a big turning point in a 26-21 Broncos win.

The Broncos got going after that. They scored two straight touchdowns to take a two-score lead.

But Denver doesn't play easy games. Carolina scored and then forced a punt after a pitch to Broncos running back Jonah Coleman was fumbled for a big loss. Denver eventually hit Bryce Young, who fumbled, and the Broncos recovered with 1:15 to go. It was another win for the Broncos, their 16th in a row in one-score games. That sets an NFL record which they tied last week when they held on in the final seconds against the Chiefs. The Broncos are 7-2, and piling up wins in close games. Per usual, they had some serendipity on their side.

Jameis Winston: He didn't start Sunday but came up with the key drive the New York Giants needed to get past the Philadelphia Eagles.

Winston came in when J.J. McCarthy briefly left the game after taking a hard hit to his side . Winston got one full drive and made it count. On the drive he completed 6-of-7 passes for 71 yards and a touchdown to Isaiah Likely. Winston also ran for 11 yards.

Offense was a struggle for the Giants all game but Winston did his job. It was the Giants' only touchdown in a 19-11 win, their first road win at Philadelphia since 2013 . They improved to 5-2-1.

Winston was benched for McCarthy as the Giants chase a division title in the terrible NFC East. But he might have been their most important player Sunday, coming through when nothing else was working for New York's offense.

Kenneth Walker III: After a couple of quiet games against very good defenses, Walker got an easier assignment Sunday. And he took advantage of it.

Walker scored two touchdowns on catches and another on the ground as the Chiefs' offense broke out in a 35-12 win over the New York Jets. He rushed for 102 yards and had another 41 receiving. It hadn't been easy for the Chiefs on the road against the Seahawks and Broncos the past two weeks, and Walker in particular was stymied. He was on a blistering pace early in the season but had just 105 rushing yards and no touchdowns the past two weeks. On Sunday he was back to his form of the first few weeks when he was getting buzz as a potential MVP candidate. The Chiefs are 6-2, and still very much in the mix for an AFC West title as long as Walker continues to play well.

Joe Burrow for MVP: The Atlanta Falcons were one of Burrow's toughest matchups in November. All he did was go 18-of-22 passing for 239 yards with two touchdowns, and one rushing TD. And that was just the first half.

Burrow's MVP push continued Sunday in Madrid as he finished with 271 passing yards and three touchdown passes in a 34-17 win over the Atlanta Falcons. He probably could have put up even bigger numbers but the Bengals were up double digits for most of the second half. The NFL Network broadcast repeatedly talked about how Burrow told them in production meetings how confident he feels and how healthy he is. It shows.

The Bengals are 6-2 and in good shape to win the AFC North, which is usually a prerequisite for winning MVP. He is putting up monster numbers. He hasn't won before and there will be some sentiment to recognize him with his first MVP award as he turns 30 years old. By the end of November he could be the clear favorite, though Josh Allen, Brock Purdy and Caleb Williams are also in the race. But Burrow is looking like the league's MVP.

Patriots secondary: The Green Bay Packers had a receiver go for 164 yards and a touchdown on Sunday, and it wasn't even the biggest receiving performance on his own team. That's how bad New England's defense was Sunday.

The Packers made it clear where the ball was going. It was either heading to Matthew Golden or Christian Watson, and usually deep. New England did nothing to stop it. Golden and Watson ran wide open in the Patriots' defensive backfield all game and Jordan Love kept piling up yards in a 45-27 win in New England .

Love was so good he was pulled early in the fourth quarter, with the Packers cruising to a blowout win. He had 372 yards and three touchdowns, riding his two red-hot receivers.

Watson had 171 receiving yards and a touchdown. Golden had 164 yards and a touchdown, including 126 yards in the first quarter.

The Packers are 6-3, and have completely turned things around since a sluggish first month of the season. Their combination of Love throwing to Golden and Watson has been devastating. Ask the Patriots, who are usually a solid defensive team. On Sunday, it was like they weren't even on the field against the Packers.

Raiders offense: The scoreboard didn't reflect it, but the Las Vegas Raiders had a chance to at least make the San Francisco 49ers sweat on the second half Sunday. But they turned it over five times after halftime.

The Raiders had six possessions in the second half and one turned out well, with a touchdown. The other five ended with three Kirk Cousins interceptions, one of which was returned for a pick-6 and another that was thrown into the end zone with the Raiders inside the 5-yard line. There were also two fumbles, one of which came right before tight end Michael Mayer was about to score, which would have cut San Francisco's lead to 28-24. The Raiders went on to lose 38-17 .

The 49ers' defense played well, as it has all season, and that's a big reason San Francisco is 7-1. But on Sunday, the Raiders played their sloppiest half of the season. It's hard to turn it over five times in one half, but Las Vegas somehow pulled it off.

Malik Willis: The whole season is a tryout for Willis, who has to prove he's worthy of being the Miami Dolphins' quarterback of the future. Sunday wasn't a good day for him.

Facing a Detroit Lions defense that isn't good and was down multiple starters due to injury, the Dolphins never reached the end zone. Willis was inaccurate on many passes. The Lions were surprisingly quiet on offense too but it didn't matter. Miami couldn't score enough to keep up and lost 19-9. Willis was 13-of-25 passing for 128 yards and an interception against a Lions defense that was 29th in yards per game allowed coming in.

Willis has had decent moments, and he has to be graded on a curve because of the lack of talent around him. But he wasn't good enough Sunday.

Deshaun Watson: Shedeur Sanders couldn't come up with the 2-point conversion he needed to close out the win over the New Orleans Saints. But he might have given the Browns a reason to consider a quarterback change.

Sanders, who threw a go-ahead 64-yard touchdown to KC Concepcion late in the fourth quarter and also led a game-tying field-goal drive in the final seconds of regulation, hit tight end Harold Fannin Jr. for a 39-yard touchdown in overtime after the New Orleans Saints scored first, with Fannin making a great play after the catch. But Sanders threw incomplete on the 2-point conversion that would have won the game (there was also a holding call on the Browns) and the Saints held on to a 23-22 win.

The loss stung but Sanders played well, as Watson sat out due to being in the concussion protocol during the week. Watson has mostly played poorly and the Browns have been winning in spite of it. Sanders had 297 yards and two touchdowns against the Saints with multiple clutch drives. It will at least be worth considering a change after that.

Sauce Gardner: His presence on the Indianapolis Colts is a constant reminder of the franchise's on-field collapse.

Last season, when the Colts were 7-2, Indianapolis traded two first-round draft picks and receiver Adonai Mitchell for Gardner, an elite cornerback. But Gardner has been mostly hurt with the Colts, who have fallen apart since the middle of last season. And on Sunday, with a chance to beat the Dallas Cowboys, Gardner got beat for the biggest play of the game.

Ryan Flournoy, playing a bigger role with George Pickens out, beat Gardner for a 46-yard catch late in the game when the Colts led 23-20. That set up a go-ahead rushing touchdown from Javonte Williams and the Cowboys' defense closed out the win when rookie safety Caleb Downs picked off Daniel Jones, who had another rough day. Dallas held on for a 27-23 win .

The Colts' fall is far from Gardner's fault, but he hasn't helped and the Colts paid way too much for him. Him giving up the game-changing catch to Flournoy was another reminder of how costly that trade was.

articles.title: Updated 2027 NFL Draft Order After Week 9 Results, Who Could Chargers & Eagles Take?
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Chargers moved one loss closer to the No. 1 overall pick in the 2027 NFL draft in Week 9.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Chargers moved one loss closer to the No. 1 overall pick in the 2027 NFL draft in Week 9.

Justin Herbert and Co. lost by double digits to the Houston Texans to drop to 0-8.

There's no end in sight right now for the Chargers, but the silver lining if they keep losing is the privilege to draft first in April.

The Miami Dolphins and Tennessee Titans are lurking at 1-7 if the Chargers do win a game at any point of the season.

The New York Jets (via the Indianapolis Colts) and the Philadelphia Eagles round out the top five in the current draft order after Sunday's afternoon games.

4. New York Jets (via Indianapolis - 2-7)

C.J. Carr delivered a statement to NFL personnel with his showing against the Miami Hurricanes.

The Notre Dame Fighting Irish quarterback threw for 319 yards and three touchdowns in one of Saturday's marquee college football games.

Carr is 25th in the FBS in passing yards and tied for ninth in touchdown passes. He's also thrown just one interception.

Carr is already in the national spotlight each week because of where he plays, but now that Notre Dame is 8-1 and headed toward the College Football Playoff, there will be even more eyes on him.

The Tennessee Titans, Miami Dolphins, New York Jets and other teams with a quarterback need should have eyes on Carr, who as of Sunday, has put himself near the top of the quarterback class that was expected to be headlined by Arch Manning and Dante Moore.

Chris Cole is emerging as one of the premier defensive prospects in the 2027 draft class.

The Georgia linebacker had nine tackles and 1.5 sacks in the Bulldogs' rout of the Ole Miss Rebels on Saturday.

Cole is now up to 58 tackles, 41 of which have been solo and five sacks in his junior season.

He could be an intriguing prospect for the Eagles and others that are looking for defensive help at the top end of the draft.

Not all of the teams in the top 10 will need quarterback help, so there's a good chance we see defensive players, like Cole, and offensive linemen shoot up the draft board in the coming months.

Jeremiah Smith still projects to be the No. 1 overall pick in the 2027 NFL draft despite the Ohio State Buckeyes' recent struggles.

Smith put up another 100-yard performance in the loss to the Oregon Ducks to bring his season total up to 1,200 receiving yards.

Smith ranks in the top five in the FBS in receptions, receiving yards and touchdowns. He'll be more than likely be a Heisman finalist.

He'd be an excellent pick for the Chargers at No. 1 because they need to revamp the offense around Justin Herbert.

The Eagles would love to have Smith as well as a complement to DeVonta Smith and Makai Lemon.

The Ohio State star ight not make it to the Eagles at No. 5 because of the Chargers' needs and potential trades up into the top five for him.

The New York Jets may also target Smith depending on how their quarterback search goes in the offseason.

articles.title: Love, Watson, Golden Dazzle as Packers Route Patriots, Box Score Stats, Highlights for Maye, More
articles.summary: Jordan Love and the Green Bay Packers stormed into Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Massachusetts, and handed Drake Maye and the New England Patriots a 45-27 loss Sunday.
articles.body:
Jordan Love and the Green Bay Packers stormed into Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Massachusetts, and handed Drake Maye and the New England Patriots a 45-27 loss Sunday.

Christian Watson and Matthew Golden powered the Packers' passing attack, combining for 335 yards and two touchdowns to help Green Bay secure the win.

The Packers entered as 3-point underdogs on the road, according to FanDuel Sportsbook , but left with a convincing win behind a dominant performance through the air and a defense that forced four turnovers.

Green Bay improved to 6-3 on the season, picking up back-to-back wins after beating the Carolina Panthers 27-19 in Week 8. Despite the victory, the Packers remain last in a competitive NFC North.

The Patriots fell to 5-4 but remain second in the AFC East, suffering their first home loss of the season.

An opening-drive interception by Maye set the tone for what would be a difficult day for New England.

Green Bay scored on its first three possessions, with Love rushing for a 13-yard touchdown and Golden hauling in a pass for another score before the Packers added a field goal to take an early second quarter 17-0 lead.

Maye threw two more interceptions in the period, giving him three turnovers before halftime. However, he countered his early struggles with two scoring drives, connecting with Rhamondre Stevenson for a 30-yard touchdown before finding Efton Chism III for another score.

Kaleb Johnson added a rushing touchdown for Green Bay to maintain the Packers' lead, sending them into halftime with a 10-point advantage.

Coming out of halftime, Green Bay's offense remained hot. Love connected with Savion Williams before finding Watson for a 39-yard touchdown on a one-play scoring drive. The Packers capped the possession with a successful two-point conversion.

The Patriots committed their fourth turnover of the game when Stevenson fumbled, but New England closed out the quarter with a score as Maye found Mack Hollins for a 22-yard touchdown pass.

New England's Corey Kiner added a rushing touchdown in the fourth quarter while the Packers were held to a field goal.

Despite trailing by as many as 28 points with just over four minutes remaining in the third quarter, the Patriots mounted a 13-3 scoring run to close out the game. However, the late surge fell short as New England ultimately lost by 18 points.

Green Bay will host the Minnesota Vikings next Sunday in an NFC North battle at 1 p.m. ET, while New England will host the Detroit Lions at 9:30 a.m. ET the same day.

articles.title: Week 10 Waiver Wire Breakout Fantasy Football Pickups from Sunday's Box Scores
articles.summary: Seth McGowan might be the most popular player in the fantasy football waiver-wire conversation going into Week 10.
articles.body:
Seth McGowan might be the most popular player in the fantasy football waiver-wire conversation going into Week 10.

The Indianapolis Colts running back could be in for a massive uptick in production if Jonathan Taylor is traded this week.

McGowan scored a touchdown and ran for 45 yards alongside Taylor in Sunday's matchup with the Dallas Cowboys.

A handful of other intriguing fantasy football options emerged in Week 9 due to injuries with their respective teams.

Shedeur Sanders sits on top of that list because he was only a few yards away from a 300-yard performance on Sunday afternoon.

Seth McGowan might be the most added player in fantasy football leagues over the next week.

McGowan is Jonathan Taylor's backup on the Indianapolis Colts depth chart. He could rise to the role of starter if Taylor is traded this week.

McGowan scored the first touchdown of his NFL career on Sunday. He picked up 45 yards on six carries.

Even if Taylor doesn't get traded, McGowan and the Colts have a good matchup on paper against the Dolphins in Week 10.

McGowan may already be off the waiver wire in some leagues because of Taylor's trade potential, but if he's still there, he's worth the pickup.

Shedeur Sanders is the Cleveland Browns backup quarterback for now.

However, Sanders showed some promise in the overtime loss to the New Orleans Saints.

Sanders threw for 297 yards and a pair of touchdowns in his first start of the season.

Deshaun Watson didn't play on Sunday, but he did clear concussion protocol, so there is a chance Watson is back on the field in Week 10 against his former team, the Houston Texans.

Houston is a tough matchup for either quarterback, but if you assume the Browns play from behind in that contest, there is a chance for a high number of pass attempts.

If anything, Sanders is worth holding on your bench for a week just in case Watson is unable to go. Cleveland does have a bye in Week 11 if it wants to be super cautious with its starting quarterback.

Omar Cooper Jr. caught eight of his 11 targets for 58 yards in a tough matchup against the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 9.

Cooper was the Jets' top target on Sunday because of Garrett Wilson's absence due to a concussion.

Even with Wilson on the field, Cooper carries a good amount of fantasy value inside the Jets offense.

The rookie out of Indiana earned five or more targets in three of his five appearances this season.

He provides Geno Smith with a trustworthy second option inside the passing game. That could be beneficial for the rest of November against an average Buffalo defense and in matchups with the Los Angeles Chargers and Miami Dolphins.

Darren Waller was a force inside the Carolina Panthers offense on Sunday.

The veteran tight end hauled in eight of his 10 targets for 90 yards and scored his second touchdown in three weeks.

Waller has had at least 50 receiving yards in two of his last three games. He's scored four times this season.

An argument can be made that Waller is the No. 2 option in the Carolina passing attack on any week because of his recent production and threat level inside the red zone.

Waller will be needed by Bryce Young in the next few weeks as the Panthers embark on a pair of divisional games to end November.

The matchups with New Orleans and Tampa Bay could suit Waller and make him one of the higher-scoring tight ends in the next few weeks.

articles.title: AFC playoff picture: Patriots hold onto wild card spot despite Packers loss
articles.summary: Assessing the AFC standings and playoff picture after the Patriots’ loss on Sunday.
articles.body:
Coming off a Super Bowl berth, the New England Patriots entered the 2026 season with some high expectations. Those have not changed, but Sunday's 45-27 loss to the Green Bay Packers showed that meeting them might become even more of a challenge than initially anticipated.

What will happen over the coming weeks and months remains to be seen, of course, but for now let's focus on the concrete impact that defeat has on the standings. And as can be seen, things could be worse.

The Patriots defending their AFC East title will be a challenge, even though they own the head-to-head advantage over the Bills courtesy of their Week 4 victory in Buffalo. However, what good is that advantage if you cannot get even in the standings? And with a fourth loss now in the books, getting even will take not just a major effort from New England but their rivals also showing some weakness.

Elsewhere in the AFC East it was business as usual. The Jets lost 35-12 to the Chiefs and are inching closer toward rebuild category once more, while the Dolphins — whose lone win this season came against New York — were once again unable to make enough plays to prevent a 19-9 loss to the Lions.

On the bubble: 8. Cleveland Browns (5-4) , 9. Las Vegas Raiders (4-5), 10. Baltimore Ravens (4-5), 11. Houston Texans (3-5)

Not yet eliminated, but let's be real here: 12. New York Jets (2-7), 13. Indianapolis Colts (2-7), 14. Miami Dolphins (1-7), 15. Tennessee Titans (1-7), 16. Los Angeles Chargers (0-8)

Even though they were dominated on Sunday, the Patriots still remain in the driver's seat for a playoff spot in the AFC. They do have multiple advantages over the only other 5-4 team in the conference, the Browns.

New England's conference record is superior, while it also owns the strength of victory and strength of schedule tiebreakers at the moment. With no head-to-head matchup on the schedule, those tiebreakers might decide who makes it to the postseason when all is said and done.

Of course, there is still a long way to go before any conversations about the playoffs become serious. For the time being, though, the Patriots are still in control of their own destiny even if they ended up ceding more ground to the other wild card competitors.

articles.title: Chiefs K Butker responds to boos heard after missed kick in Week 9
articles.summary: See how Chiefs kicker Harrison Butker reacted when he was asked about the boos that were heard after his latest missed FG at Arrowhead Stadium.
articles.body:
Veteran kicker Harrison Butker has struggled to find his rhythm during the 2026 NFL regular season, and Kansas City Chiefs fans appear to have reached their limit with the three-time Super Bowl champion.

After Butker missed back-to-back field goal attempts in the second quarter of Kansas City's Week 9 win over the New York Jets, a noticeable chorus of boos was heard from the crowd at Arrowhead Stadium.

While both of Butker's misses were from a distance of more than 50 yards, his latest debacle put him atop the NFL's leaderboard in missed field goals this season and may be the final straw in deciding his fate moving forward.

Take a look at this video of Butker's response to the boos sent his way by fans on Sunday, which was posted to Twitter by the official account of Sports Radio 810 WHB:

"I'm booing myself sometimes," Butker can be heard saying near the end of the clip. "It's just... people are passionate, the fans are passionate. They want to win games. They want me to make kicks. I want to make kicks. It's part of it. That's what you sign up for, and I've got to be better."

The Chiefs signed Butker's tentative replacement — former Baltimore Ravens boot Justin Tucker — but head coach Andy Reid told the media that he is "not making any decisions" about the kicker position in the immediate aftermath of Kansas City's victory over the Jets.

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes returns from elbow injury scare to lead Chiefs past Jets, reportedly has clean MRI
articles.summary: Mahomes looked like he may have sustained a significant injury but was able to return on the next Kansas City possession.
articles.body:
Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes left Sunday's game against the New York Jets with an injury scare after a hit to his throwing elbow but was able to return to help lead a 35-12 win.

After the game, NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported that Mahomes underwent a postgame MRI that did not reveal a major injury.

The hit took place in the second quarter on a sack that forced a fumble. Mahomes' right elbow bent awkwardly on the sack, and he fumbled the ball. He was in clear pain after the hit and walked to the sideline holding his right arm. The Jets took over possession after recovering the fumble.

But Mahomes was able to throw on the sideline and returned to the field before the end of the half after the Chiefs retook possession of the ball.

Kansas City took over with 32 seconds remaining in the half after a missed Jets field goal and Mahomes was able to complete a 12-yard pass, then scramble for seven yards to set up a Harrison Butker field-goal attempt just before the end of the half.

Butker missed the 51-yard attempt, and the Chiefs went into halftime with a 14-12 lead.

"He hurt his elbow a little bit," head coach Andy Reid told CBS at halftime. "It's sore, but he came back. He's a tough kid."

Mahomes continued to play to start the third quarter and led the Chiefs to a touchdown drive on their first possession of the half to extend their lead to 21-12. The Jets didn't mount a challenge from there.

Mahomes didn't appear to be impacted by the injury scare and finished the day completing 230of-31 passes for 278 yards (7.8 yards per attempt) with 2 touchdowns and no turnovers.

"If I'm able to play, I'm going to play," Mahomes said after the game. "In scares you in moments when you get pains in certains areas of your body, so obviously I didn't feel great. I was able to get it worked on a little bit, especially at halftime, and was able to go out there and play the rest of the game."

Mahomes said he felt good after the game. "I'm sure I'll be sore tomorrow, but we'll get right to it and work on it."

The Chiefs improved to 6-2 with the win and remain a half game in the AFC West behind the Denver Broncos, who improved to 7-2 with a 26-21 win over the Carolina Panthers.

articles.title: The Packers can (sometimes) solve all their problems with Jordan Love deep balls
articles.summary: What the Packers did to Christian Gonzalez was technically bullying.
articles.body:
America's Game of the Week wasn't the tense shootout Fox hoped when it put Tom Brady back in the booth for a return to Foxborough. The Green Bay Packers and New England Patriots were both 5-3. They both had young, emerging quarterbacks with dynamic deep balls and uneven performances. The potential for an instant classic shootout was high.

Jordan Love showcased all the qualities that make him an MVP candidate by thoroughly dismantling the Patriots secondary. He threw for 335 yards ... to wideouts Christian Watson and Matthew Golden alone . The young veteran's day was done by the early fourth quarter in a 45-27 win that proved the Packers will be, at the very least, an incredible headache in the NFC playoff race.

There were several factors that went into the rout were visiting fans made "go Pack go" chants audible on the broadcast minutes before Rob Gronkowski was celebrated in the Patriots Hall of Fame. Evan Williams and Xavier McKinney led a lights-out defense that forced four turnovers and could be one of the league's best units once Micah Parsons is healthy.

But the bigger deal is what the Green Bay offense can be at the peak of its powers.

Jordan Love didn't back down from the Patriots stars. His young receiving corps stepped up alongside him

Red flags abounded in Green Bay's Week 7 loss to the Detroit Lions . The Packers squandered a chance at a key road win against a division rival thanks in large part to a litany of catchable passes that wound up on the turf . Through eight weeks, his receivers were averaging nearly three drops per game, most in the NFL .

Love made a statement in Week 9. Not only did he trust his wideouts, but he relied on them to beat the league's highest paid cornerback like a rented mule's dusty rug.

The Packers didn't avoid Christian Gonzalez. They exploited him instead . The All-Pro corner was the frequent victim of big throws to Watson and Golden en route to their historic days. These weren't near misses or lucky bounces; Green Bay receivers beat him consistently to get to perfectly placed balls.

Love threw 14 passes that traveled at least 10 yards downfield in his three quarters of heavy(ish) lifting. He completed 10 (with one throwaway) for 295 yards, a pair of touchdowns and zero interceptions. That's more than 21 yards per attempt and a 153.3 passer rating on what should have been his toughest throws of the day.

The added benefit of those vertical routes is the space it creates. Obviously that's a boon for Tucker Kraft's routes. It also generates single coverage for the latest link in the franchise's neverending chain of mid-round draft pick wideouts to thrive. Just look at this Savion Williams touchdown!

But the best example of this may have been a routine third down conversion. On third-and-seven from the Green Bay five-yard line, Watson lined up across from Gonzalez with a safety shaded over the top. Both defenders were prepared for a long vertical route. Instead, Watson snapped off an out-breaker and picked up his 10 easiest yards of the day (in a play I didn't clip, because it's fairly common but still appreciated).

That's the beauty of this offense. Being able to consistently make deep shots work opens up every aspect of the field. Cornerbacks default to turn-and-run mode. The split second of recognition that a short throw is coming creates the space for easy gains. Occasionally, those turn out to be highlights, too!

All told, Love turned 29 passes into 372 yards and three touchdowns. This was MVP-caliber play that puts him in the same air as Trevor Lawrence, Joe Burrow and Josh Allen halfway through this season. Sure, it came against a Patriots defense that ranked firmly in the middle of the NFL pack when it came to expected points added (EPA) allowed , but it was the same tune he'd been singing throughout the 2026 season. There will be mistakes throughout, whether it's drops or the imperfect passer trying to do to much and throwing the dumbest pass you've ever seen about one in 50 tries.

But on Sunday, Green Bay proved it can beat anyone in the NFL. And there may be some unexpected support.

The Packers might be able to run the ball (or maybe that's an outlier)

Green Bay rightfully has little faith in its run game. The Packers had eschewed third-and-short runs for screen passes, play-action or gadget plays multiple times the last few weeks, including late in the second quarter when Savion Williams took a backward pass for a loss of one on third-and-2.

But even with Josh Jacobs sidelined after the first quarter, Green Bay's run game showed signs of life. The savior came from an unlikely place. Kaleb Johnson was the Pittsburgh Steelers' seventh-string running back in the preseason, one year after being the team's third-round draft pick.

He had only 26 carries over the team's first eight games, occasionally breaking free for chunk runs but being largely ineffective. His 32.1 percent success rate (a measurement of the yards gained during a play and how it sets the offense up for first down conversions) ranked dead last among all tailbacks with at least 25 carries.

On Sunday, he posted career highs of 14 carries and 68 rushing yards. The Packers topped 70 rushing yards for only the second time all season and broke the 100 yard barrier for the first. Jacobs gained only five yards on four carries before leaving with a broken finger, but Johnson and Pierre Strong were able to provide a run game that was still below average but wasn't terrible. That's progress!

New England held four of its last five opponents to fewer than 100 rushing yards. Its 3.8 yards allowed per carry ranked 10th in the league. They should have feasted against the Packers but instead let them look like a normal offense.

Getting any kind of clock-burning, tough-yard-getting presence would be vital to the team's postseason success; especially if that means not having to rely on Tucker Kraft on third-and-inches.

The Packers' top 10 defense created havoc and stopped Drake Maye in his tracks. The offense picked on the league's highest-paid cornerback so savagely it could technically be considered bullying. And now the run game might not be a full-on embarrassment. That could be all Green Bay needs to shake off its postseason malaise under Matt LaFleur.

articles.title: How Browns got a glimpse at future of pass-catching group in OT loss
articles.summary: The Browns got massive plays from KC Concepcion, Denzel Boston and Harold Fannin Jr. in their overtime loss to the Saints.
articles.body:
NEW ORLEANS ― It was exactly what the Browns hope it would look like. All three of Denzel Boston, KC Concepcion and Harold Fannin Jr. making huge plays for an explosive offense.

There were only two big problems. The first was that it didn't fully coalesce until there was almost no time remaining in their game at the New Orleans Saints .

The second, and bigger, issue? It happened in a 23-22 overtime loss to the Saints .

Cleveland Browns vs New Orleans Saints. Best photos from Week 9 NFL game

Boston and Concepcion were just in their ninth game of their first season in the league, while it's just the second season for Fannin. Yet, they combined 12 catches for 225 yards and two touchdowns in the loss.

"I think, you know, we have a great passing attack over here with the Cleveland Browns ," Boston said. :You know, I think definitely something to look forward to. At the same time, I don't think we should use that as an excuse for not being able to win games. I think that we got to go out and play our very best every single game that we play. It's a week-to-week league, and us being young shouldn't reflect on our record. I think we're all grown men, so we go out there and play the game at our highest level."

All three were on the receiving end of a new quarterback, at least for this week. Second-year pro Shedeur Sanders started in place of Deshaun Watson, sidelined due to being in concussion protocol during the week, and completed 19-of-31 passes for 297 yards and two touchdowns.

However, it was when Sanders shined the most, especially in the final 5:30 of regulation and all of overtime, that the three young pass catchers seemed to glow the brightest. Concepcion had a 64-yard touchdown with 521 remaining in the fourth quarter to give the Browns a 13-9 lead.

It was Concepcion's first NFL touchdown. It also came after he limited off the field and into the medical tent with a right ankle injury, which he returned from to start the fourth quarter on a punt return.

"Like I said before, I play with so much passion," Concepcion said after catching four passes for 85 yards in the game. "I play with so much grit. I play with so much dawg. So as soon as it happened, I went to the blue tent. I got taped up good and tight. I was ready to go."

That was one of two 60-plus-yard completions for Sanders in the second half. The other was 61-yard catch-and-run that Boston made a terrific adjustment on the ball while it was in the air to get it over Saints cornerback Kool-Aid McKinstry.

Boston was also central to what could've been the winning play, the two-point conversion in overtime. He tried to do the scramble drill with Sanders, who was flushed out of the pocket by New Orleans' Carl Granderson, but couldn't come up with the football.

A holding penalty on right tackle Tytus Howard would've negated the try even if Boston would've caught it.

"It was close," Boston said after catching six passes for 98 yards. "I think it just became a scramble drill play and we weren't able to get it done. Even if we did hit it, we still had a holding call in play, so it would have been canceled and negated anyways, which sucks. But, you know, we're just trying to fight every single down that we play and try to put our best foot forward."

The two-point conversion play came after Fannin had entered the group chat, so to speak. The tight end didn't get so much as a target through four quarters, but had two receptions on two targets in overtime for 41 yards.

Those 41 yards included a 39-yard catch and run where Fannin ran a crossing route, stiff-armed two Saints defenders before turning and stumbling his way up field all the way into the end zone for a touchdown. It was the ultimate quality over quantity day for him.

"Yeah, I mean, I was just really going out there, not doing any thinking, just reacting," Fannin said. "I just told them, like, it was like a flash. Like, I don't know. I didn't even realize what I was doing until after the play was over, you know? But, yeah, just had to make a play for my teammates and things like that. It was a good play."

articles.title: Andy Reid declines to rule out Chiefs kicker change another missed Harrison Butker FG: 'I need to see it go through'
articles.summary: Will Justin Tucker replace Butker as Kansas City's kicker?
articles.body:
Kansas City kicker Harrison Butker missed another field goal Sunday, his only attempt of the day in a 35-12 win over the New York Jets .

The miss ramped up pressure on the veteran kicker, who's facing competition from the Kansas City practice squad via eight-time All-Pro Justin Tucker .

Butker's miss Sunday was from 51 yards as the first-half clock expired. It prompted boos from the Kansas City crowd and a question from CBS' Tracy Wolfson to head coach Andy Reid about what he needs to see from Butker moving foward. His answer was succinct.

"I need to see it go through," Reid said.

After the game, Reid didn't wait for a question to address Butker and Kansas City's kicking situation. He brought it up during his opening statement.

"I'm sure I'll be asked about Butker," Reid said. "I'll address that as we go throughout the week. I'll look at everything. No need to ask. That'll be the answer that you get.

"Not making any decisions right now today."

So there is a decision to make. And Reid is clearly not ruling out making a change.

Butker is in his 10th season with the Chiefs and has won three Super Bowls with the team. A decision to move on from him won't come lightly.

He's in the midst of the worst season of his career by far. With Sunday's miss, Butker is 12 of 19 for the season. His 63.1% conversion rate trails his single-season career low of 88.6% last season by a wide margin.

The Chiefs, meanwhile, brought in Tucker for a reason.

Tucker comes with a significant amount of baggage due to 16 allegations of sexual misconduct against him from his time with the Baltimore Ravens. It's not the sort of baggage a team would be expected to take on for somebody to sit on the practice squad.
